messages:
Maria R.: Heads-up — planning a canary comparison/dashboard set for the next Dedicated rollout. We need runtime + infra telemetry contract updates so the console can surface per-canary regressions (latency, token cost, quality proxies). Can teams list required signals, tag names, and sampling constraints?

Jason T.: For basic comparative dashboards we should emit: p50/p95/p99 latency, p999 (for outliers), request_error_rate (4xx/5xx), model_fallback_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_utilization, tokens_per_request, tokens_per_second, and cost_per_token. Also need low-cardinality tags: route, model_variant, canary_id, env.

Lee (eng-platform): +1. Naming conventions: use route_id, model_version, canary_label. Add request_id and trace_id for correlation. For privacy, if we want quality signals, emit response_hash (sha256) and confidence_score instead of raw text. Also we should emit is_canary=true/false and canary_group (A/B buckets).

Sarah (product): Product asks for A/B comparison metadata: experiment_bucket, baseline_version, and window_start/window_end on events so the dashboard can compute lift and run stats. Also define alert thresholds (e.g., p95 latency delta > 20% for 10m).

infra-bot: Deploy: canary rollout canary-2026-03-27-7 started on pool-dedicated-3 (cc @eng-platform).

Jason T.: Example telemetry event we should standardize (draft):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-27T14:12:33Z",
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "trace_id": "trace_...",
  "route_id": "generate.text.v2",
  "model_variant": "gpt-like-q4_1",
  "canary_id": "canary-42",
  "is_canary": true,
  "canary_group": "grpA",
  "latency_ms": 142.3,
  "tokens_in": 12,
  "tokens_out": 84,
  "kv_cache_hit": true,
  "status_code": 200,
  "cost_microcents": 18,
  "response_hash": "sha256:...",
  "quality_score": 0.73
}
```

Maria R.: Two operational asks: 1) High-cardinality tags (customer_id, full model_path) will blow up metrics storage — prefer emitting low-cardinality tags for metrics and include full metadata in sampled traces/logs. 2) Need a sampling strategy for raw event emission (suggest: 1% raw event sample overall + 100% for errors).

Lee (eng-platform): Agreed. For metrics keep histograms for latency and counters for rates. We'll expose bucketed_latency_ms histogram and aggregated kv_cache_hit_rate and fallback_rate per route/canary. For detailed analysis we rely on sampled traces (trace_id present).

Sarah (product): Dashboard ask (wireframe): side-by-side baseline vs canary panels with delta column and significance flag. Panels: latency percentiles, error_rate, tokens_per_request, kv_cache_hit_rate, fallback_rate, cost_per_token, and sample response_hash table. Also a metric showing percent of requests routed to canary over time.

Maria R.: Also need routing policy metadata emitted when a decision occurs: route_policy_version, routing_reason (latency|cost|region), fallback_policy. That lets us correlate regressions with policy changes. Timeline: aim to start emitting contract fields next Tue; sampling + dashboards the week after.

Jason T.: I'll open the telemetry-spec PR today with the JSON schema and a Grafana dashboard stub (will link here). Planning to add lint/job to validate new telemetry event fields.

Maria R.: Awesome — thanks. Please tag the PR with "canary-telemetry" and @eng-platform for review. :thumbsup:

Jason T.: Will do. Linking draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/telemetry-specs/pull/789 (WIP)

Maria R.: Great. I'll sync with infra on storage/cost limits. If anyone has objections to the sampling numbers, voice them here before EOD.

Sarah (product): No objections from product. Keep us posted on alerts/thresholds so we can tweak.

Lee (eng-platform): I'll add the histogram buckets proposal to the PR.

infra-bot: Note: metric cardinality increase may trigger retention policy alerts; infra will monitor.

Maria R.: Thanks everyone — follow-ups in the PR thread.
